ref: Bloom, B. H. (1970). Space/time trade-offs in hash coding with allowable errors. CACM 13(7).
title: Bloom filter
summary: A bit array with several hash functions answers set membership queries: hash each item into the bit array, set the bits; a lookup checks the bits. Probabilistic: false positives are possible, false negatives are not.

ref: IEEE 802.3 truncated binary exponential backoff; also AWS Architecture Blog 'Exponential Backoff and Jitter' (2015).
title: Exponential backoff with jitter
summary: After a failed request, retry after a delay that doubles each time, with a random jitter offset so many clients do not retry at the same moment.

ref: Karger et al. (1997). Consistent hashing and random trees. STOC.
title: Consistent hashing
summary: Place servers and keys on a ring by hashing them; each key goes to the next server around the circle, so adding or removing a server moves only a few keys (minimal remapping).

ref: Mohan et al. (1992). ARIES. ACM TODS 17(1).
title: Write-ahead logging
summary: Record every change in an append-only log on disk before applying it to the data, so after a crash the system can replay the log to recover.

ref: Shapiro et al. (2011). Conflict-free replicated data types. SSS.
title: CRDTs
summary: Replicated data types whose merge operation is commutative, so replicas can apply changes in any order and still converge without coordination: conflict-free merge of copies.

ref: Fidge (1988); Mattern (1989). Vector clocks / version vectors.
title: Vector clocks
summary: Each replica keeps a vector of logical clock counters to tell whether one version happened before another or whether they are concurrent.

ref: Token bucket algorithm (e.g. RFC 2697/2698 traffic metering).
title: Token bucket rate limiting
summary: Tokens refill a bucket at a fixed rate; each request spends a token, so throttling caps the requests per second while allowing short bursts.

ref: Merkle, R. (1987). A digital signature based on a conventional encryption function. CRYPTO.
title: Merkle tree
summary: A tree of hashes where each parent stores the hash of its children, so two copies can find which parts differ by comparing hashes top-down.

ref: Michie, D. (1968). Memo functions and machine learning. Nature 218.
title: Memoization
summary: Cache the results of a function call keyed by its arguments and reuse earlier results when the same inputs come again.

ref: Horizontal partitioning (sharding), e.g. Bigtable (Chang et al., OSDI 2006).
title: Sharding
summary: Split the data into partitions by key range or hash and place each partition on a different machine to spread load.

ref: Dijkstra, E. W. (1959). A note on two problems in connexion with graphs. Numerische Mathematik 1.
title: Dijkstra's shortest path
summary: Find the shortest path in a graph of nodes and edges with non-negative weights by repeatedly expanding the closest unvisited node.

ref: Soil-moisture-based irrigation controllers (e.g. EPA WaterSense-labeled soil moisture sensors).
title: Soil-moisture irrigation controller
summary: Sensors measure soil moisture and the controller skips or schedules watering of the field only when the soil is dry.

ref: Content-addressed deduplication, e.g. restic / borg backup.
title: Content-defined deduplication
summary: Split data into chunks, hash each chunk and store each fingerprint only once, removing duplicates across backups.

ref: Command pattern / undo stacks (Gamma et al., Design Patterns, 1994).
title: Undo stack
summary: Keep a stack of reversible commands so the user can revert or roll back the last changes.
